discovery: Room-temperature tunnel magnetoresistance and giant TMR in crystalline MgO magnetic tunnel junctions

nominees.name: Shinji Yuasa
nominees.affiliation: National Institute of Advanced Industrial Science and Technology (AIST), Japan

motivation: In 1995 Miyazaki and Moodera independently showed large tunnel magnetoresistance at room temperature in ferromagnet/insulator/ferromagnet junctions, turning a low-temperature curiosity into a usable spin-dependent quantum tunnelling effect. In 2004 Yuasa achieved giant TMR using epitaxial crystalline MgO barriers, confirming the coherent, symmetry-filtered tunnelling predicted theoretically and raising magnetoresistance to hundreds of percent. Together these discoveries founded the magnetic tunnel junction as the central element of modern spintronics. MTJs replaced GMR sensors in hard-disk read heads within a few years and now form the storage cell of spin-transfer-torque MRAM, which is produced in commercial foundries as non-volatile, energy-efficient memory. They are also enabling new paradigms such as probabilistic and neuromorphic computing. This is a fundamental quantum-mechanical spin phenomenon that has become a global technology, which is exactly the kind of achievement the Nobel Prize in Physics recognizes.
